screen: /start, Documents to More context (partial): browser Back, rail Library, reload, closed page, new browser profile
title: Leaving Start a run part-way, by browser Back, the rail's Library link, a reload or a closed page, throws away the whole form, and the page gives no warning and no way to resume it.
expected: An analyst who leaves a four-step form holding uploaded documents, answers and a pathway can come back to it, or is warned before it is lost. PRODUCT.md Operating Context (the analyst uploads documents, picks a pathway, reviews and submits); control-matrix CT-006 (documents and answers are the user's decision and are kept until Submit); apps/issuer-library/README.md 'Starting a run on an issuer' (the page keeps and shows a submitted run's state).
actual: With three documents read, Full credit assessment chosen and a note typed on step 3 (More context), browser Back went to the Library home, because the four steps share one address. Forward, the rail's Library then Start a run, a reload, a closed page reopened as a new tab and a brand-new browser profile each opened a blank Documents step: no files, the default issuer, no message that a draft ever existed. No 'leave this page' dialog was shown. Nothing is kept in local or session storage. The three uploaded files stay on the service unreferenced (seen under the probe's own run root). After Submit, browser Back from the run page also opens a blank form.
suggested_change: Keep the draft (step, answers and file list) in the submission the page already creates and restore it on return, or warn on leaving; give each step its own history entry so Back goes to the earlier step.

title: Start a run opens with an example issuer already typed into the required Issuer name and Issuer ID fields, and today's date as the case date.
expected: Required fields start empty, with example text only as a placeholder, so the analyst chooses the issuer. control-matrix CT-001 (Issuer name: the user's, required) and CT-003 (case date: the user's); the Your name field already does this with the placeholder 'Eric G'.
actual: On first load, before anything is typed, Issuer name holds the value 'Northbridge Group', Issuer ID 'northbridge-group' and As-of date today's date (2026-11-17); all three are required, none is a placeholder. The values come from the example context file cases/context/research-minimal.json, which the service loads in both synthetic and regular mode (react_frontend/__init__.py:397; the file's own as_of is 2026-10-31). An analyst who fills the documents and goes on without retyping files the run under the example issuer; the form shows no mark that these are defaults.
suggested_change: Open the form with empty required fields and use the example only as placeholder text (for example 'Northbridge Group plc').

title: An unreadable document is reported as a raw Python decoder error for one file only, and no row is marked, so the analyst cannot tell which of several files is the problem.
expected: The page lists each document with those it ignored and why (control-matrix CT-006); the analyst needs no knowledge of launcher or code messages (PRODUCT.md Users); rubric D-31 'no raw error string'.
actual: Inspect on a mislabelled PDF, a truncated workbook and a good filing gave one red line, "Cannot read annual-report.pdf: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x89 in position 0: invalid start byte". The workbook was not mentioned (alone it gives the same kind of codec text), every row including the good filing still read 'Selected' and Documents inspected stayed 'Not met'. The analyst must remove a file, inspect again and meet the next one. The browser console logs 'Launcher flag not shown to the analyst: --sources: ...' for each, so the page treats the text as not for the analyst yet draws it.
suggested_change: Mark each unreadable row ('Cannot be read: not a PDF'), list every problem at once, and replace the decoder text with one plain sentence.

title: Two files with the same name are kept as two identical rows and refused only at Inspect with 'Choose documents with distinct file names.', which names no file.
expected: The row of a document the page cannot use says which it is and why (control-matrix CT-006; rubric D-16 specific copy); two buttons do not share one accessible name.
actual: Choosing northbridge-filing.txt twice made two identical rows with two identical 'Remove northbridge-filing.txt' buttons and no mark. Nothing happened until Inspect documents, which showed 'Choose documents with distinct file names.'; no row is marked and nothing offers to drop the repeat.
suggested_change: Refuse or mark the repeated name when it is chosen ('Same name as the row above') and name the file in the alert.

title: A second copy of the same document under another name (for example 'northbridge-filing (1).txt') is accepted as a separate document with no flag.
expected: The page lists documents it ignored and why (control-matrix CT-006); a repeated document is called a repeat.
actual: The same filing bytes under two names gave '2 documents inspected, 0 ignored.' with both rows 'unrecognised'; the review sheet's 'Documents read' listed both. Whether a live run would read the filing twice was not verified (R4); in the synthetic test the extra file fails the run (J2-014).
suggested_change: Compare content hashes when files are added and mark a repeat 'Same content as <name>'.

screen: /start, Documents step (error and partial, after Inspect documents)
title: A wrong file type is accepted for upload and described two different ways, and neither says why or which types are read.
expected: The page lists documents it ignored and why (control-matrix CT-006).
actual: A .exe alone gave 'The uploaded documents: no readable issuer file' and stayed 'Selected'; beside a good filing the same file and a .png read 'Ignored / Will not be read' with '1 document inspected, 2 ignored.' The drop zone says only 'Add filings and other source documents. Up to 50 MB per file.'; the file input has no accept list; no text names the types that are read or why a file 'will not be read'.
suggested_change: Name the readable types beside the drop zone and give each ignored row a reason ('Not a document type the run reads').

title: An empty file is reported as 'Empty.txt has no extractable text (scanned image?)': the file name's first letter is capitalised and the hint suggests a scanned image for a 0-byte file.
expected: Copy quotes the file name as it is and says what is wrong (rubric D-16 plain, specific copy).
actual: Choosing empty.txt (0 bytes) alone and inspecting gave 'Empty.txt has no extractable text (scanned image?)'. The row stayed 'Selected'; the analyst's file name is not 'Empty.txt', and a file of 0 bytes is empty, not a scan.
suggested_change: Quote the name unchanged and say 'empty.txt is empty (0 bytes)'; keep the scanned-image hint for files that have bytes and no text.

screen: /start, Review and start after 'Edit purpose and modules' (full)
title: Changing the purpose after approving clears the approval and every limit decision, and the review sheet never says that this happened or why.
expected: Editing after approval invalidates the approval (control-matrix CT-031) and the analyst is told so, so they know why they decide again (PRODUCT.md Principle 2: a limit is a decision the analyst makes).
actual: After approving a Full assessment with three limits accepted (Readiness 'Decisions made 3 of 3', 'Summary approved Met') the analyst pressed 'Edit purpose and modules', chose Lite and returned to Review run. The sheet showed approval unticked, 'Decisions made 0 of 2', Submit disabled and '2 decisions left before you can approve.' Nothing says the earlier approval and decisions were cleared or that the change caused it. The behaviour itself is correct and kept the analyst's note, rating and agreement choice.
suggested_change: Add one sentence at the top of the sheet when a change cleared an approval: 'You changed the purpose, so the approval and your decisions were cleared. Decide again.'

title: A run that stopped offers no retry or resume; its one control, 'Start from this run', opens a new submission and the page does not say so, and the README calls the control something else.
expected: control-matrix CT-038 (resume of an interrupted or capped run: CP-OS resumes, the user relaunches into the same folder, 'no page control found'; an owner matter); apps/issuer-library/README.md ('a failed, capped, rejected or interrupted run's progress view offers "Start again from this run"'); PRODUCT.md Principle 2.
actual: The Failed run page shows a red Failed chip, the reason 'launcher exited 2; see logs/<id>.log' (that log answers 404), 0 of 5 or 14 modules 'Not run', and one header button, 'Start from this run'. No page text says retry, resume, try again or restart. The button opens /start?from=<id>: a new submission with today's date, an empty name and an empty file list until Inspect documents (J1-015). The stopped run stays Failed; the screen does not say that the new run is separate, has its own cap, or whether anything is reused. Why the run failed is J3-002 and J1-003.
suggested_change: Label the control as the README does ('Start again from this run') and add one line saying it begins a new run with its own cap; whether to add a retry or resume control is the owner's decision.

title: A Failed run's Activity feed never records that the run stopped: its newest entry still reads 'Running, Run started.'
expected: Run states are shown on the run page (control-matrix CT-035) and what a run could not do is stated, not hidden (PRODUCT.md Positioning).
actual: On the Failed page the chip and a reason box say Failed, but the Activity feed lists only 'Running / Run / Run started.' above 'Queued / Ana L / Run registered.' No entry says the run stopped or why; 'Report' and every module read 'Not run'.
suggested_change: Add a closing feed entry such as 'Run failed' with the reason.

title: Two runs of the same issuer, date and pathway started together are both accepted and finish, and the library then lists two identical history rows, each called the first run, with nothing to tell them apart.
expected: A run says when it was made and what it compared with (control-matrix CT-028; apps/issuer-library/README.md 'Which runs are listed': runs sharing a date are all marked and counted); the Start page says when the issuer already has runs (README 'Starting a run on an issuer').
actual: Two tabs prepared Northbridge Synthetic Group, 2025-03-31, Full credit assessment; both sheets were approved before either run existed, and the two were confirmed 0.2 s apart. Both ran side by side and finished in about 4 s. Library home shows one card '2 runs'. Report history shows two rows, both 'Full credit assessment / As of 31 March 2025', with no run id, time or submitter, and only one with a 'Finished' chip. Each run's Changes says 'No earlier run to compare. This is the first listed run for this issuer on this pathway.' A second same-issuer run started after the first finished fails instead (J3-002), so the outcome depends on timing. The analyst paid for the same slot twice and the screens cannot say which report is which.
suggested_change: Show the run's start time and submitter on each history row and Changes line; say on Start and in the Submit dialog that this issuer has a run in progress. Whether to block the second run is the owner's decision.

title: Typing an issuer that already has runs shows no notice on Start a run; the earlier runs are looked up only when the analyst presses 'Carry over from latest run'.
expected: apps/issuer-library/README.md 'Starting a run on an issuer': 'The start page also says when a typed issuer ID already has runs (and, if the typed name differs from the filed one, shows the filed name)'.
actual: With one finished run for northbridge-synthetic-group, typing the issuer name by keyboard (the ID followed) and the analyst name, then waiting 2 s, showed no notice and made no request to /api/issuers/<id>. The request was made only when 'Carry over from latest run' was pressed. While a first run was still running, the page also said nothing; only Run activity ('Running 1') showed it. The first warning is the review sheet's 'Changes: Compared with the Full credit assessment run as of 2025-03-31' on step 4.
suggested_change: Look the issuer up when the ID changes and show 'This issuer has N runs, the latest as of <date>' under the field.

screen: /start, Review and start, after the Submit request fails (error)
title: When the Submit request fails, the dialog closes and the message is drawn 2,900 px above the Submit button, so the analyst sees nothing change and cannot tell whether the run started.
expected: An error is an alert the analyst can see, with an action, and no raw error string (rubric D-31); 'Retrying Submit run is safe.' is meant to be read (control-matrix CT-037); status messages reach the analyst (rubric D-43).
actual: With the connection dropped once during the Submit request, the confirmation dialog closed, focus returned to 'Submit run', and the alert 'Failed to fetch Retrying Submit run is safe.' sat at y=-2912 px with the page scrolled to the button (viewport 900 px). A screen-reader user hears it; a sighted analyst sees nothing. 'Failed to fetch' is the browser's own text. Pressing Submit again started exactly one run.
suggested_change: Draw the message beside the Submit button (or scroll to it and move focus to it) and replace 'Failed to fetch' with 'The page could not reach the service. Nothing was started.'

screen: /start review sheet then /run/<id> (synthetic test, error, Failed)
title: In the synthetic test, one document more than the three Northbridge files (a re-downloaded copy or any other file) is read, summarised and approved, and the run then ends Failed with no reason the analyst can act on.
expected: A synthetic Submit starts the synthetic engine and spends nothing (control-matrix CT-033); docs/react-workflow.md 'Open the interface' names the files; the sheet itself says 'The synthetic test uses the supplied documents'. A refusal is stated before Submit, not after.
actual: Adding 'northbridge-filing (1).txt' (same bytes) to the three case files gave a review sheet that listed four documents with no warning. Submit ended 'Failed', 0 of 14, 'launcher exited 2; see logs/<id>.log' (the log answers 404). The launcher's own log reads 'synthetic proof requires exactly one northbridge-filing.txt upload and at most its workbook and credit agreement'. A non-duplicate extra file (other-note.txt) failed the same way. Proof-service behaviour only; the live page was not exercised (R4). Same message family as J3-002 and J1-003.
suggested_change: State on the synthetic review sheet which files it accepts, and let the launcher's one-line reason reach the run page (one fix with J3-002).

screen: /runs and /run/<id> (partial, a run waiting behind three running)
title: A run that waits behind three running ones is listed under Waiting and shown as Queued with no reason, no limit and no position.
expected: apps/issuer-library/README.md 'Waiting runs': a run waits when 3 are going; Run activity lists it under Waiting and says why; status changes are explained (rubric D-43).
actual: Four runs confirmed within 0.6 s gave 'Running 3, Waiting 1'. The Waiting table has two columns (Issuer, Pathway); the run's own page says 'Queued', 'Elapsed n.a. not available', 'No start time recorded'. Nothing says three runs are going, that this is a limit, or what it waits for, so a waiting run cannot be told from a stuck one. It did start when one of the three ended (about 5 s) and finished.
suggested_change: Add one reason line to the Waiting row and the run page: 'Waiting: 3 runs are going (the limit). It starts when one ends.'

screen: /report/<id> opened while the run is still going (error)
title: The report address of a run that is still going says 'The published report could not be loaded.' and not that the run is still running.
expected: Loading, empty and error states are designed and say what is true (rubric D-31).
actual: Opening /report/<id> 0.8 s after Submit gave 'Credit report / The published report could not be loaded.' (the service answered 404 'unknown report' for /connected/snapshot?run=<id>, one console error). The same address loaded the full report once the run had ended. The 'Open report' link appears only after publication, so the analyst meets this through a copied or bookmarked address, which is how a person returns after leaving.
suggested_change: When the run is not finished, show 'This run is still going' with a link to its Run activity page.
